summary: Plus-addressing email variants cause JIT elevation approval links to be unrecognized
description: Issue summary: Several support engineers report that Just-In-Time (JIT) elevation approval emails are being delivered to users but the approval service rejects the approval tokens when the user's Okta profile contains a plus-addressing variant (user+alias@example.com). Impact: Affected support and SRE staff cannot complete runbook elevation from approval links in email; manual escalation required for affected users. Scope: Intermittent — appears for ~3% of elevation request attempts over last 48h, concentrated on users who have email aliases with a plus sign in Okta and who are routed through our legacy approval link encoder.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In Okta, confirm a user has an email profile with a plus sign (e.g., alice+infra@company.com) and that the primary email is the plus-addressing variant.
2) From the internal console, request JIT elevation for that user to execute a runbook that requires approval.
3) System sends approval email with a click-through link to the user’s email address.
4) Click the approval link (desktop mail client -> browser).
5) Observe the approval service returns an error page: 'Approval token not recognized' and the console shows the elevation pending with no change in status.
observed_behavior: Approval emails are delivered to the user (verified via mail headers and user confirmation).
Clicking the link opens console but approval service logs 'token validation failed: identity mismatch'.
Affected users must escalate to on-call to manually grant temporary elevation.
expected_behavior: Approval link should validate the token and complete the elevation flow for any email alias that the user owns, including plus-addressing variants.
No manual intervention required if user clicks the email link within SLA window.
logs: 2026-03-13T09:14:22Z approval-service ERROR token_validation: uid mismatch (expected: alice@company.com, observed: alice+infra@company.com) request_id=req-6b2f1
2026-03-13T09:14:22Z console WARN elevation_flow: approval_link_clicked user=alice+infra@company.com ip=18.204.12.33
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: token payload includes a normalized email (stripped plus) but approval link encodes the raw email address, causing mismatch during validation.

Checked SCIM profile data: Okta primaryEmail is 'alice+infra@company.com'. Our identity-proxy normalizes some addresses (lowercase + strip tags) for older tenants but not consistently across all codepaths.
Replayed a failing approval event in staging with identical inputs: reproduced token_validation error when email normalization flag differs between approval-link-encoder and approval-verify service.

Related code paths: approval-email-generator (legacy) URL-encodes the raw email into 'user' param; approval-verify service compares against normalized identity from idp-claim (which strips plus-address tags for some orgs).
No changes to Okta or SES observed in the time window; spike correlates with a rollout two days ago that reintroduced legacy encoder behind a feature flag for a subset of requests.

resolution: Fix in progress: centralize email canonicalization in identity-proxy and update approval-email-generator to use canonicalized address when generating/encoding approval tokens.
